title: Administrative Assistant
company: Oxford University Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust
advertiser_name: Oxford University Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust
description: This is a 12-month fixed-term Band 3 Administrative Assistant post providing maternity leave cover within the Psychological Medicine Service. The role is responsible for delivering a comprehensive, professional and efficient administrative service that supports clinicians and the wider multidisciplinary team in providing high-quality patient care. The post holder will manage patient administration throughout the patient pathway, including appointment booking, referral processing, reception duties, Electronic Patient Record (EPR) management, production of clinical correspondence, maintenance of accurate patient records, and supporting compliance with Trust and national performance standards. The role is fundamental to ensuring the smooth day-to-day operation of the service and maintaining a positive patient experience. Provide a comprehensive administrative service to support the Psychological Medicine Service and multidisciplinary team. Manage patient pathways by processing referrals, booking appointments and maintaining accurate patient records using the Trust's Electronic Patient Record (EPR) systems. Provide reception cover, acting as the first point of contact for patients and visitors, delivering a professional and compassionate service. Produce and process clinical correspondence using digital transcription systems, ensuring Trust timescales and quality standards are met. Monitor and manage shared email inboxes, process incoming correspondence and respond to patient, referrer and stakeholder enquiries promptly and appropriately. Support Referral to Treatment (RTT) pathways by ensuring accurate data entry, clinic preparation, patient check-in/check-out and clinic cash-up processes. Maintain high standards of data quality, confidentiality and customer service while supporting the smooth day-to-day running of the department. Work collaboratively with clinical and administrative colleagues, contributing to service improvement initiatives and providing flexible administrative support to ensure continuity of patient care MAIN PURPOSE OF POST: Patient administration underpins the patient journey and supports the clinical teams in delivering high quality patient care and can make a real difference to the patient experience. Effective and efficient patient administration supports the management team to deliver a high standard of data quality by making the best use of capacity and resources. The post holder is responsible for the delivery of a professional, comprehensive and efficient administrative service to support the delivery of high quality clinical services under the supervision of the Senior Administrator. Administration: To provide primary administrative support to the clinical staff and all patients under their care of The Psychological Medicine Service, including using EPR applications, such as Appointment Book, HIM Tracking, HIM Chart Coding, Powerchart and PM Office, to manage patient pathways. To provide reception cover and act as the first point of contact for patients attending face to face appointments and meeting and greeting patient Ensuring the waiting room area is kept clean and tidy. 4. To manage an electronic diary room booking system. 5. Dealing with incoming correspondence, opening and prioritising incoming post, ensuring supporting information is available when appropriate and taking responsibility for actioning items in a timely manner. 6. To monitor the shared e-mail inbox, taking responsibility for forwarding emails, creating encounters and uploading referrals to EPR for triaging and forwarding to relevant consultant through the EPR Message Centre. 7. To ensure appointments are booked into the appropriate clinic appointment slots in line with the Trusts Elective Access Policy and local Standard Operating Procedures in order to meet national RTT Standards, and following the appropriate escalation process to highlight problems to the Assistant Service Manager and / or the Operational Service Manager when in need of assistance. 8. Use of the digital transcription system (Voice Recognition) to produce clinical correspondence to inform referrers, patients and other stakeholders of patient pathway progress. In doing so, produce high quality accurate correspondence which conforms to the Trust Key Performance Indicator of 7 working days from the point of clinical delivery/decision to being sent to the patient. 9. Liaising with referrers to ensure effective pathway management and to maintain good working relationships with stakeholders. 10. Become proficient in the use of Scan IT software to ensure letters, clinical reports, diagnostic test results and other notes are uploaded and filed correctly in patient records on EPR. 11. Check in patients attending for their Psychological Medicine appointment, checking demographic information such as name and date of birth are correctly recorded in EPR and updating with changes and corrections. 12. Check out patients from their appointment, following the instructions on the outcome form to ensure the correct RTT status code is recorded. 13. Cache up clinics regularly to ensure revenue is accurately captured. 14. Complete the e-clinic-prep process to ensure relevant documentation is present on EPR for patient appointments. 15. Follow the HIM tracking procedure for the movement of all paper patient notes. 16. Act upon queries from referrers, patients and other stakeholders in a timely manner. Take relevant action to provide reassurance and support to patients and their families by finding appropriate solutions to problems. 17. Escalate any problems arising to Assistant Service Manager or Operational Service Manager in a timely manner so they can be dealt with quickly and efficiently. 1. Demonstrate high levels of customer care and be an ambassador for customer care within the Trust. 2. Attend Departmental meetings and training as required to ensure that you maintain an up-to-date working knowledge of service and Trust procedures. 3. Provide a robust administration function that underpins the delivery of a high quality service and maintain effective working relationships with clinical, nursing and administrative staff. 4. Answer all telephone calls in a timely manner and action appropriately 5. Maintain patient confidentiality at all times . 6. Be flexible in your approach to work, such as covering other job roles at an appropriate grade or site, and to include varying working hours to ensure the service maintains a minimum level of cover during its core hours. 7. Use the Trust IT systems to register patients, make appointments, produce end of treatment letters, ensure that details are correct and ensure check in / check out of outpatient appointments. 8. To support and contribute to on-going and future service development projects supporting continuous improvement of the services we provide. 9. Any other duties at the request of the Senior Administrator/Service Manager, which may be needed to fulfil the objectives of the post, which are appropriate to the grade. This job description should be regarded only as a guide to the duties required and is not intended to be definitive. It may be reviewed in the light of the changing circumstances following consultation with the post holder. The job description does not form part of the contract of employment . The management of risk is the responsibility of everyone and will be achieved within a progressive, honest and open environment. Staff will be provided with the necessary education, training and support to enable them to meet this responsibility. Staff should be familiar with the Major Incident Policy Fire Policy and should make themselves familiar with the local response plan and their role within that response. The post holder is responsible for ensuring that all duties and responsibilities of this post are carried out in compliance with the Health & Safety at Work Act 1974, Statutory Regulations and Trust Policies and Procedures. This will be supported by the provision of training and specialist advice where required. Infection Control is everyones responsibility. All staff, both clinical and non-clinical, are required to adhere to the Trusts Infection Prevention and Control Policies and make every effort to maintain high standards of infection control at all times thereby reducing the burden of Healthcare Associated Infections including MRSA. All staff employed by the OUHFT have the following key responsibilities: Staff must decontaminate their hands prior to and after direct patient contact or contact with the patients surroundings. Staff members have a duty to attend mandatory infection control training provided for them by the Trust. Staff members who develop an infection (other than common colds and illness) that may be transmittable to patients have a duty to contact Occupational Health. The post holder will endeavour at all times to uphold the rights of children and young people in accordance with the UN Convention Rights of the Child. The Trust is committed to safeguarding children and vulnerable adults throughout the organisation. As a member of the trust there is a duty to assist in protecting patients and their families from any form of harm when they are vulnerable. All staff must complete annual information governance training. If you have a Trust email account this can be completed on-line, otherwise you must attend a classroom session. For further details, go to the Information Governance intranet site. Data quality is a vital element of every member of staffs job role. The Oxford Radcliffe Hospitals recognises the importance of information in the provision of patient care and in reporting on its performance. Data quality is therefore crucial in ensuring complete, timely and accurate information is available in support of patient care, clinical governance, performance management, service planning, and financial and resource planning and performance.

title: Accounts Assistant
description:
Robert Half are delighted to be partnering with a small, ambitious and friendly business based in Oxford. They are looking for an Accounts Assistant to take ownership of an important part of the financial operation.

This is a fantastic opportunity for someone with finance experience who enjoys variety, likes working with people as well as numbers, and wants to play a genuinely meaningful role within a growing, close-knit business.

The Role

Reporting into the finance team, you will play a key role in ensuring customer accounts are accurately maintained and payments are received and allocated promptly. You'll be working with customers from around the world across multiple currencies, and the role goes well beyond routine accounts receivable. You'll also liaise with sales and marketing colleagues, resolve customer queries, produce reports, and get involved in wider business projects.

Key responsibilities include:
- Allocating customer payments accurately against invoices and reconciling bank accounts
- Preparing and importing bank statements into Xero
- Proactively chasing outstanding debts by phone and email, maintaining accurate records of collection activity
- Managing the accounts receivable inbox and resolving customer queries promptly and professionally
- Producing and reviewing the monthly Aged Debtors Report
- Maintaining and updating debt-tracking spreadsheets and reports
- Supporting the wider finance function with ad hoc projects and administration

About You
- Previous experience in an accounts receivable, credit control or accounts assistant role
- Confident working with multiple currencies and reconciling accounts
- Strong communication skills, with the confidence to proactively chase payments
- Organised, accurate and comfortable managing a varied workload
- Experience with Xero (or similar accounting software) is desirable but not essential

What's on Offer
- Salary of up to £32,000, depending on experience
- Hybrid working - 3 days in the office, 2 days from home
- Discretionary annual bonus
- 25 days' holiday plus bank holidays, rising with service (up to 30 days)
- Early finish on Fridays
- Company pension scheme
- Quarterly team socials and Christmas party
- Free on-site parking
- The chance to join a small, fun team with genuine international reach

Apply Now

If you're looking for a varied finance role within a supportive, sociable team where you can make a real impact, we'd love to hear from you. Apply today or contact Robert Half's Oxford office for a confidential conversation.

Robert Half Ltd acts as an employment business for temporary positions and an employment agency for permanent positions. Robert Half is committed to diversity, equity and inclusion. Suitable candidates with equivalent qualifications and more or less experience can apply. Rates of pay and salary ranges are dependent upon your experience, qualifications and training. If you wish to apply, please read our Privacy Notice describing how we may process, disclose and store your personal data:

title: Accounts Payable Clerk
description:
The Accounts Payable Clerk will focus on managing and processing invoices, ensuring payments are made accurately and on time. This role in Oxford supports the smooth financial operations of a not-for-profit organisation.

A not-for-profit organisation based in Oxford.

Description
- Process invoices and ensure accurate data entry into the accounting system.
- Reconcile supplier statements and resolve any discrepancies promptly.
- Prepare and process payment runs in a timely manner.
- Maintain accurate records of all accounts payable transactions.
- Communicate effectively with suppliers to address and resolve queries.
- Assist with month-end closing activities related to accounts payable.
- Support the team with ad hoc finance-related tasks as required.

Profile

A successful Accounts Payable Clerk should have:
- Previous experience in accounts payable or a similar role in accounting and finance.
- Strong attention to detail and accuracy in processing financial data.
- Proficiency in using accounting software and Microsoft Excel.
- Good communication skills for liaising with suppliers and internal teams.
- A proactive and organised approach to managing tasks and meeting deadlines.

- Hourly rate of £13.00-£18.00, dependent on the level of experience.
- Temporary contract with the opportunity to make a valuable contribution to a not-for-profit organisation.

title: Commercial Property Secretary
company: Macildowie Recruitment and Retention - Agency - Permanent
description:
Macildowie are working with this client based in Oxford to recruit an experienced Legal Secretary to join their Commercial Property team.

Legal Secretary - Commercial Property

Location: Oxford
Salary: £30000
Contract: Permanent
Working Arrangement: Hybrid and Flexible

This is an excellent opportunity to join an established professional services organisation, providing high-quality secretarial and administrative support to a busy team of property specialists.

You'll be working closely with fee earners, helping to ensure commercial property matters progress smoothly and clients receive a professional and responsive service. It's a varied position where organisation, accuracy and the ability to juggle competing priorities will be key.

What will you be doing?

You'll provide comprehensive secretarial and administrative support, including:
- Creating, formatting and amending legal documents and correspondence
- Producing accurate documentation from digital dictation
- Preparing leases, reports and other property-related documents
- Managing diaries, meetings and day-to-day administration for fee earners
- Opening, maintaining and closing client and matter files
- Liaising professionally with clients, agents, solicitors and other external parties
- Supporting commercial property transactions with searches and documentation
- Assisting with Land Registry and Companies House documentation
- Supporting Stamp Duty Land Tax returns, completion paperwork and post-completion administration
- Assisting fee earners with time recording, billing and routine accounting queries
- Scanning, printing and preparing documentation for signature

What are we looking for?

You'll be highly organised, accurate and comfortable working in a fast-paced professional environment.

Previous legal secretarial experience would be highly desirable, with experience supporting Commercial Property or Real Estate teams particularly advantageous.

You'll also need:
- Excellent organisational and time-management skills
- Strong written and verbal communication
- Excellent attention to detail
- Good IT literacy and confidence learning new systems
- Experience working with document and/or case management systems
- The ability to manage multiple priorities and deadlines
- A professional and client-focused approach

If you're an experienced Legal Secretary looking for your next opportunity in Oxford, we'd be keen to hear from you.

Please apply with your latest CV for further information.

Macildowie is a specialist recruitment consultancy with a rich history of enhancing the careers of professionals across the Midlands and Northern Home Counties. We have an unrivalled understanding of the local market and are dedicated to helping you achieve your career aspirations.

title: Service Advisor
description:
Service Advisor - Oxford

Location: Oxford

Salary: £30,000 - £38,000 OTE

Job Type: Full-Time, Permanent

About the Role

We are looking for a professional and customer-focused Service Advisor to join a busy and successful aftersales team in Oxford. Acting as the key link between customers and the workshop, you will ensure every customer receives exceptional service while supporting the efficient operation of the service department.

This is an excellent opportunity for an experienced Service Advisor or a customer service professional with automotive experience who is looking to develop their career within a reputable dealership environment.

Key Responsibilities
- Greet customers and manage service and repair bookings.
- Accurately record customer concerns and vehicle requirements.
- Liaise with workshop technicians regarding vehicle progress and additional work requirements.
- Provide customers with updates throughout the repair process.
- Prepare and explain service invoices and associated costs.
- Promote and sell additional aftersales products and services where appropriate.
- Ensure all administrative tasks are completed accurately and on time.
- Maintain high levels of customer satisfaction and retention.
- Handle customer queries and complaints professionally and effectively.
- Work closely with colleagues across the service and parts departments.

Requirements
- Previous experience as a Service Advisor, Customer Service Advisor, or similar customer-facing role within the automotive industry.
- Strong communication and interpersonal skills.
- Excellent organisational and administrative abilities.
- Ability to work effectively in a fast-paced environment.
- Experience using dealership management systems is advantageous.
- Strong attention to detail and customer-focused approach.
- Full UK driving licence preferred.

What's on Offer
- Competitive salary package with realistic OTE of £30,000 - £38,000.
- Manufacturer and in-house training.
- Career development opportunities.
- Pension scheme.
- Employee discounts and benefits package.
- Supportive and professional team environment.
- Modern dealership facilities.

Ideal Candidate

The successful candidate will be passionate about customer service, highly organised, and capable of building strong relationships with customers and colleagues alike. You will take pride in delivering an excellent customer experience while helping the aftersales department achieve its performance objectives.

Salary: £30,000 - £38,000 OTE

Location: Oxford

Position: Full-Time, Permanent

Industry: Automotive Aftersales / Service Department
